newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian police arrest Turks for heroin smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Romanian police arrest Turks for heroin smuggling.

text.p: Romanian police said on Friday they had seized 42 kg (92 pounds) of heroin, the biggest drug haul in Bucharest in seven years, and arrested two Turks on charges of smuggling it into the country.

"Police of the capital's fifth district caught red-handed a Turkish coach driver and his helper while they were putting 84 packages of pure heroin into two bags," Bucharest deputy police chief Ion Dan, told a news conference.

Dan said the heroin, worth the equivalent of $2 million, had been hidden aboard a coach taking Romanian tourists to and from Turkey. Police allowed the vehicle to cross into Romania and take its passengers to the capital then pounced on the two men when they returned to retrieve the packages.
If convicted, the pair face up to life in prison. Dan said one of the accused was an addict exhibiting severe withdrawal symptoms.
Since the 1989 fall of communism, Romania has become a favourite drug transit point, made popular by lax anti-drug laws and the closing of Yugoslav routes during the Bosnia war.
Police have seized 13.5 tonnes of drugs in seven years and authorities have tightened provisions of the criminal code.
Hard drug use is not yet widespread in Romania, where average monthly salaries are less than $100, and police said the heroin was almost certainly bound for elsewhere.
